applicable_failures: The initial candidate scan failed with a Python SyntaxError (first bash call), so it produced no inventory result until a rerun.

The successful scan appears filename/path-term filtered rather than a complete metadata review: its visible output includes 1001-00003 (asset-purchase-agreement), 1001-00006 (earnout-tax memoranda), and 1001-00007 (stock-purchase-agreement), which are apparent non-Capital-Markets false positives.
Candidate matters were not comprehensively listed: the TSV shows multiple files only for 1001-00003 and other matters, but no subsequent all-file listing call is shown.

Several surfaced candidates were not screened by document reading; for example, 1001-00003, 1001-00004, 1001-00006, and 1001-00007 appear in the TSV, but no read call opens documents from those matters.
critique.concerns: The stage established many plausible Capital Markets matters and opened useful governing/status documents, including executed, dormant, withdrawn, and draft matters. However, the evidence does not establish a complete, reliable candidate set from all 266 matters. The 63-line filename-oriented output contains obvious transactional false positives, while many surfaced matters were neither fully file-listed nor opened. Thus the claimed completeness and exclusion of unrelated matters are unsupported.
critique.recommendation: Use the existing TSV only as a starting index. For every one of its candidate matter numbers, systematically list the complete matter folder, then identify and read the governing agreement plus execution, closing, withdrawal, or dormancy proof. Reconcile all 266 inventory entries against that ledger, explicitly retaining or excluding each candidate with a document-based reason; do not rely on filename hits alone.
